newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel weighs release of Hamas founder -Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Israel weighs release of Hamas founder -Netanyahu.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday that Israel was considering freeing the spiritual leader of the Islamic militant group Hamas but had made no commitment to do so.

"We did not commit ourselves at any stage on the freeing of Sheikh (Ahmed) Yassin. We are always checking the issue based on his illness. We are weighing the issue but there were no commitments," Netanyahu told reporters at national police headquarters.
"In contrast, there were obligations towards freeing of female (Palestinian) prisoners in the framework of the agreement. But a specific date was not set and it will certainly be set in the future."

It was not clear which agreement he was referring to. Israel reaffirmed its commitment to release Palestinian prisoners in a deal clinched last week that led to the transfer of 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule on Friday.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, on his triumphal entry to Hebron on Sunday, said Israel would "soon" release the wheelchair-bound Yassin. Arafat said the women prisoners would be released in a few days. Israel holds some 5,000 Palestinian prisoners. About 20 are women.

Israeli Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said after visiting Yassin, 60, in December that there was room to discuss freeing him. Yassin, paralysed and in poor health since an accident when a young man, was jailed by Israel for life in 1989 on charges of founding Hamas.

Hamas has led violent opposition to interim Israel-PLO peace deals struck since 1993. It shook the peace process to its foundations with four suicide bombings over nine days last February and March that killed 59 people in Israel.
Differences have appeared in Hamas between between moderates and those pushing violence. Yassin is considered a moderate.
